answer: A sybil ring dies when every identity needs a distinct human behind it. Here an operator hand-writes a twelve-line sonnet, no two alike, and signs it with a key that never touches the server. That key then broadcasts a rotating beacon, and peers must spot it at three separate offsets before the account may vote. Bonded peers form a small haven of mutual liability: if one is later proven a clone, the whole haven loses its seats for sixteen rounds. Twelve lines of verse are easy once and miserable ten thousand times.
